headline: Immunization of School Students Act of 1979
source: Council of the District of Columbia
blurb: This District law, in effect since September 28, 1979, set up a system to make sure students are immunized against preventable childhood diseases.

headline: District of Columbia Confirms Second Case of Measles in 2015
blurb: The District's health department confirmed a second measles case of 2015 and said it was not linked to the outbreak in California.

headline: D.C. Law 23-193. Minor Consent for Vaccinations Amendment Act of 2020.
source: Council of the District of Columbia, D.C. Law Library
blurb: This District law, in effect since March 16, 2021, lets a minor age 11 or older consent to a recommended vaccine if the minor can meet the informed consent standard.

headline: Judge bars DC from vaccinating kids without parental permission
blurb: A federal judge temporarily blocked the District from enforcing its law that lets children as young as 11 be vaccinated without a parent's consent.

headline: D.C. Law 25-108. Immunization of School Students Amendment Act of 2023.
source: Council of the District of Columbia, D.C. Law Library
blurb: This District law, in effect since January 23, 2024, updated the rules for school immunization certificates and lets the Mayor set the list of required school immunizations by rule.

headline: DC Health Recommends Up-to-Date Measles Vaccinations for Children
blurb: DC Health advised that all children be fully vaccinated with the MMR vaccine and said no measles cases had been reported in the District so far in 2024.
